panels.description: One row per node per problem, which is what the list below is bounded to 200 of. If this reads higher than 200, the list is showing the worst slice and this tile is the true total, so the list is not the whole story. **Unless Nodes Withheld reads above zero**, in which case this tile is short too: that cap sits upstream of the union this counts, so the dropped nodes never reach it.

panels.title: Nodes In Scope
panels.description: Nodes PuppetDB knows about in the selected PE and environment. The denominator: Nodes Needing Work against this is the health of the estate.

panels.title: Nodes Withheld
panels.description: Nodes off the PCP broker beyond the per-scrape cap of 200, dropped before the work list is built. **Above zero, every tile and the table on this board are short by this many**, including Work Items, which is otherwise the honest total when the list below is bounded. Zero is the answer on any estate with fewer than two hundred disconnected nodes, which is nearly all of them.

The node name links through to its own board. Work Items above is the true count: when it reads higher than this list is long, the list is the worst slice.

panels.title: Excluded From Alerting
panels.description: Nodes set to alert level none, and so left out of every fleet ratio and every count on this board and the NOC. Not a fault: silencing a node is a deliberate decision. It is here because the effect is invisible everywhere else, since those tiles read the same whether the silenced machines are healthy or broken.

panels.title: Which Nodes, And At What Level

defaults.noValue: No node carries an alert level

panels.description: Every node carrying an operator-set alert level, and which level. Empty is the common case. A node at level none contributes to the tile beside it and to nothing else anywhere; the other levels are what the per-node severity rules fire on.
